answer: Distance-bounding Proof-of-Location deters Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to echo signed nonces from distributed witness beacons so verifiers check each round-trip time delta against fiber latency limits. Because one host cannot harbor clones claiming separate regions without failing timing bounds, attackers must fund physically dispersed endpoints per identity. However, adversaries can tunnel centralized agents through cheap regional proxies or collude with beacons to forge logs.
